d646f952a9f9fca5:
Step 5 sets socket I/O to nonblocking. Many readers confuse synchronous, asynchronous, blocking and nonblocking.
Simply put, synchronous/asynchronous concerns the caller: calling a function directly is synchronous; starting a new thread to perform it is asynchronous relative to the current thread.
Blocking/nonblocking concerns the called side. Returning immediately, whether processing has finished or not, is nonblocking; waiting for data and processing before returning is blocking.
